title: The Last Inch Above the Bins
premise: The camera studies the gap between the cargo stack and the roof. One shallow bag moves, and the rest of the episode admires the inch it freed up.

title: A Flat Tray Under a Deeper Crate
premise: We slide one shallow tray beneath a taller supply crate, then check whether the trunk still closes. The arrangement changes very little, which is also the episode's conclusion.

title: The Bin That Only Fits Sideways
premise: One plastic bin is rotated through its two possible orientations while the camera holds on the trunk opening. It fits either way, and the family declines to develop a position on the question.

title: Where the Lids Go
premise: The camera follows unattached storage lids as they are stacked, moved, and stacked again beside their containers. By the end, all the lids are together and nobody needs one.

title: A Cardboard Divider Has a Short Career
premise: A flattened shipping box separates two supply bins, then gets folded flat so the bins can sit together. The camera records the brief career of a divider that never quite divides anything.

title: The Slight Slope at the Back of the Trunk
premise: An empty tote slides toward the hatch, gets moved back, and slides again. We keep filming the cargo floor long after the tote has made its point.

title: The Bag Inside Every Other Bag
premise: The camera follows folded reusable totes nesting into one larger tote, then shows the bundle tucked between hard-sided containers. It occupies almost no more room than a bag full of bags deserves.

title: The Crates Change Shape as Supplies Run Down
premise: As supplies run down, half-empty boxes sag and stop stacking square. The family repacks the trunk around the new gaps, and the load slowly takes the shape of what's left.

title: Tall Stack or Wide Footprint?
premise: The same sealed containers go up in a tall column, then get spread flat across the cargo floor. The tower saves floor space right up until someone needs the bottom crate.

title: The Trunk Stops Being a Puzzle
premise: Every stop starts with unloading half the trunk to reach one kit. The family films a full unload and reload, puts tomorrow's needs nearest the hatch, and gets ten minutes of every stop back.
